newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Swiss Clariant posts 29 pct net rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swiss Clariant posts 29 pct net rise.

text.p: Swiss speciality chemicals group Clariant AG, spun off by Sandoz ahead of its merger with Ciba as pharma giant Novartis, on Friday said 1996 net profit soared 29 percent to 137 million Swiss francs ($95.5 million).

"The main factors were improved cost structures and more dynamic business in the second half (of 1996) as well as favourable exchange rates," Clariant said in a statement released before its annual news conference.

Clariant's board proposed a dividend of 10 Swiss francs per share for 1996 results as against 4.50 francs for the second half of 1995, its first period of independence after being spun off as of July 1995.

Clariant said sales rose nine percent to 2.33 billion Swiss francs despite stiff global competition in its main businesses -- textile, leather and paper dyes and chemicals as well as pigment/additives and so-called masterbatches.
"The operating margin also rose from 9.8 percent to 10.1 percent," it said.
It said operating profit rose 11 percent last year to 235 million Swiss francs.
"The operating profit improvement also continued in the first two months of 1997," it added but did elaborate.

Clariant's debut in 1995 was followed last year by a another Swiss chemicals newcomer, Ciba Specialty Chemicals AG, also born of a spin-off ahead of the mega-merger between Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz as the world's biggest pharmaceuticals and life sciences group.

Clariant plans to grow by taking over the specialty chemicals business of German pharmaceutical group Hoechst AG, a proposal that will be submitted to the Clariant annual shareholder meeting on April 29.

The Clariant board has already agreed to the deal announced last December after Hoechst agreed to sell its specialty chemicals business and to take a minority stake in the expanded Swiss group. ($ = 1.434 Swiss Francs)
